label: fact
about: The wind the airports reported (METAR) during Storm Charles, from 10 November 18:00 UTC to 12 November 12:00 UTC, resolved onto each runway end as headwind (negative: tailwind) and crosswind, joined per hour to the airline departures OpenSky's receivers saw and to ANA's own cancellation figures. Facts: the METAR (IPMA's observations) and the counts as their sources give them; the components are arithmetic on the METAR (wind speed x cos/sin of the angle between wind and runway, true degrees). Hypothesis, labelled where it appears: which runway end the wind favours (air traffic control chooses the runway, and pilots and airlines apply their own limits; we state none). Departures are a floor: what OpenSky saw, only for hours its rolling window covered.
not_a_warning_service: Not a warning service. No forecast or advice of ours. Your airline decides whether your flight runs: its site or app has the latest. For warnings follow IPMA and ANEPC.
attribution: The OpenSky Network, https://opensky-network.org (M. Schäfer, M. Strohmeier, V. Lenders, I. Martinovic, M. Wilhelm, "Bringing Up OpenSky: A Large-scale ADS-B Sensor Network for Research", IPSN 2014). Used for research and non-commercial purposes, as its API documentation asks; its full terms page is still for a person to read (transport/sources.md).
METAR: IPMA, through the US NOAA Aviation Weather Center (aviationweather.gov), public domain.
Cancellations: ANA Aeroportos de Portugal, newsroom figures only, with the link.

units.wind: knots (1 kt = 1.852 km/h); direction: degrees true the wind blows from
units.components: knots; crosswind_from: the side of the aircraft the wind comes from, landing or taking off on that runway end

departures.paused: read under OpenSky's terms, now paused pending a licence (Dinis) (from 2026-11-11T22:26:56Z): OpenSky's terms of use, as quoted by incident.flights@ from a read at 22:19 UTC (flights/sources.md), require OpenSky's written licence for use of its REST API in any live product, service or automated system, and limit use to non-profit research and education. Our hourly reader is automated. The terms page answered 403 to our own read at 22:26 UTC, so a person has to read it. Paused, as Metro de Lisboa was at 12:08, until Dinis decides.

departures.note: departures_seen on each hour: OpenSky's count for that hour on the day transport's file covers; null where not covered (10 November, and the hours before the first reading)

sources.what: runway headings, degrees true (OurAirports, public domain; read once, cached)
METAR, IPMA's observations through the US NOAA Aviation Weather Center's public API (public domain)
airline departures per hour (OpenSky) and ANA's figures, kept by incident.transport@

source: https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar (IPMA's METAR), with incident.meteorologist@'s airport files; runways from OurAirports
method: For each METAR: headwind = wind x cos(wind direction - runway heading), crosswind = |wind x sin(...)|, true degrees; gust components the same with the gust. hours[] (LPPT) and hours_by_airport give, per hour, the METAR with the strongest gust or wind. Variable winds (VRB) have no components.
